title: Hepatoprotective and neuroprotective effects of quinacrine against bile duct ligation-induced hepatic encephalopathy in

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods – biochemical assay kit descriptions (ALP and ALT paragraphs)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same catalogue number 'A526' is used for two different, unrelated assay kits from two different manufacturers: 'Serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP) concentration was ascertained by use of a colorimetric assay... provided by BioAssay Systems... (catalogue No. A526)' and later 'the serum levels of aspartate transaminase (AST) and alanine transaminase (ALT) were determined following the instructions provided by TECO DIAGNOSTICS... (catalogue No. A561 and A526, respectively).' A single catalogue number cannot correctly identify kits from two distinct vendors (BioAssay Systems vs. TECO Diagnostics), indicating a transcription/attribution error in the methods section.

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods – serum ammonia and bilirubin assay section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'The concentration of serum total ammonia and total bilirubin were quantified... Values were expressed as mmol/ml and mg/100 ml, respectively.' Serum ammonia is physiologically present at micromolar concentrations (even in hepatic failure models, typically tens to a few hundred µmol/L); reporting it in 'mmol/ml' (equivalent to mol/L) would correspond to concentrations many orders of magnitude higher than biologically plausible, indicating an incorrect/implausible unit for this measurement.

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods – MDA and GSH assay section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states MDA and GSH were measured and 'reported in units of (nmol/mg protein) and (pg/mg protein), respectively.' Tissue GSH concentrations are typically in the nmol/mg protein (or µg/mg protein) range; reporting GSH in picograms per mg protein would be several orders of magnitude lower than physiologically expected values, suggesting an implausible/incorrect unit.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 8 (behavioral assessment timeline) vs. Sections 9–11 (OF, MWM, NOR test descriptions)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 8 states: 'At the completion of the experiment on day 28, the animals underwent behavioral assessments on day 29 and day 30.' However, the detailed test descriptions contradict this: the Morris water maze training occurred 'for a duration of four days (from day 25 to 28)' and the NOR habituation phase occurred on 'day 26 and 27' with training on 'day 28' — i.e., behavioral testing actually began on day 25, well before the stated 'completion of the experiment on day 28' and the claimed day 29–30 assessment window, creating an internal timeline contradiction.

Quinacrine-treated groups (3, 4, 5) received daily intraperitoneal injections for 28 days ('Quinacrine was dissolved in distilled water... and injections began on the same day as the surgery'), but the sham (Group 1) and BDL (Group 2) groups are not described as receiving any vehicle (distilled water) injections. This omission of a vehicle-injected control introduces a potential confound (daily injection stress/handling) between drug-treated and untreated groups that is not addressed in the design.
